topics.topic_title: Images in Two Inclined Plane Mirrors

notes_list.title: Number of Images: n = 360/theta
notes_list.basic_overview: For two plane mirrors inclined at angle theta: if 360/theta is even, n = 360/theta - 1. If odd and the object lies symmetrically, n = 360/theta - 1; if odd and asymmetric, n = 360/theta. If it is a fraction, take only the integer part.
notes_list.extra_info_content: Quick table: 30 deg - 11, 45 deg - 7, 60 deg - 5, 120 deg - 2, 180 deg - 1, 0 deg (parallel mirrors) - infinite. Example: theta = 72 deg, object unsymmetrical, so n = 360/72 = 5.

notes_list.title: Mirrors: Basic Facts
notes_list.basic_overview: The first mirror (silvered glass mirror) was made by German scientist Justus von Liebig, who coated glass with silver metal.
notes_list.extra_info_content: Concave mirror: inner surface of a sphere is the reflecting surface. Convex mirror: outer surface is the reflecting surface.
